Machine-Readable Metadata of a DMAR Result, and the Classes of Its Refusals

Source: R/dmar_metadata.R
dmar_metadata.Rd

Returns, in one list with fixed names, what a program built on DMAR needs to read beside the numbers of a result table: which estimator, standard errors, test, and missing data method produced it; which version of a fit measure was reported and what corrected it; how many cases and groups it rests on and, after two-stage estimation, how many rows each stage read; which auxiliary variables entered; whether the result is fully eligible or qualified by an unavailable unrestricted (H1) model; and the counts of a bootstrap. Every DMAR table already carries these as attributes, but under names that differ by family; this accessor reads them into one stable vocabulary, so that an application reads dmar_metadata(x)$eligibility$status rather than the attribute of the day. A field a result does not have is NULL.

Usage

dmar_metadata(x)

Arguments

x

A result table of a DMAR function (a dmar_tbl).

Value

A named list with the fields above; a field the result does not carry is NULL.

Details

Fields

result

The table's own class, the first element of class(x) ("dmar_sem_fit", "dmar_reliability", "dmar_fa_confirmatory", and so on), and coefficient, the reliability coefficient a reliability table reports.

estimator, se_method, test

The point estimator, the method of the standard errors, and the test statistic actually used, as the function recorded them: lavaan's names for a fitted model ("ML", "robust.huber.white", "satorra.bentler (scaled)"), the reliability family's names for its own ("analytic"). The fit measure families record lavaan's point estimator ("ML" for a fit requested with estimator = "MLR", whose robustness is in se_method and test); the information criteria record the estimator as requested ("MLR").

missing

The missing data method as the function recorded it: lavaan's names for a fitted model ("listwise", "ml", "two.stage", "robust.two.stage") and DMAR's for its own arguments ("fiml", "two_stage", "robust_two_stage", "pairwise", "none" or "covariance input" for a supplied matrix).

ci_method, wald_df, conf_level, rmsea_conf_level, tail_areas, denominator

How an interval was formed: the method, the degrees of freedom of a Wald interval (Inf for the normal), the level, the level of the RMSEA interval, unequal tail areas when recorded, and the denominator of an omega. rmsea_conf_level is the level the table records for its RMSEA interval apart from its other intervals, 0.90 by default (the fit rows of fa_confirmatory, cfa_1, cfa_2, fa_bifactor, and fa_second_order, whose parameter intervals are at conf_level, the fit line of fa_exploratory, and the fit measures of irt_grm), or else, for a table whose RMSEA interval is its own (sem_fit_measures, factor_count, ci_rmsea, equivalence_rmsea), the table's level; it is NULL for a table with no RMSEA interval.

interval_degenerate

For a table of an order-based effect size (vargha_delaney_A, cliff_delta, probability_of_superiority_paired) whose estimated variance is 0, so that its two limits equal the estimate and are not a confidence interval: "complete_separation" or "no_variation". NULL for a table with an interval.

version, version_reason, correction

For a fit measure table, the version reported ("standard", "scaled", "robust"), why, and the correction behind a robust version, from the sem_fit attribute (the information criteria of sem_information_criteria record under sem_information, read the same way).

N, groups, fit_rows

The cases the result rests on, where the function records them (an attribute, or the N row of a reliability table), and the number of groups; after two-stage estimation, fit_rows is the record of the rows the first stage read and lavaan counted in each group, how many were observed on an auxiliary variable alone, and whether the fit was computed again with all of them (read, nobs, extra, corrected, which is NA when no case was observed on an auxiliary variable alone, and reestimated, whether that computation estimated a model that links the groups again).

auxiliary

The auxiliary variables of a FIML or two-stage fit, where the function recorded them.

eligibility

A list with status, code, and note: "eligible" when nothing qualifies the result (code and note then NULL), and "qualified" with a code and the text of the warning the function gave: "h1_unavailable" when the unrestricted (H1) likelihood was unavailable and the constrained model's estimates were retained with their H0-based uncertainty, and "two_stage_rows_unavailable" when a two-stage fit whose first stage read cases observed on an auxiliary variable alone could not be computed again with every case, so that its standard errors and the values that rest on lavaan's N are qualified (see Refusals for the cases where nothing is returned).

bootstrap

For a bootstrap result, a list with B (attempted), used, failed, improper, and, where the family records them, the finer counts of the reliability engine (returned, undetermined, not_converged, too_few_cases), with required, the fewest replications a request may ask for, and status, one of "complete", "dropped", "exploratory", "insufficient_count", or "insufficient_share" (see dmar_bootstrap).

simulation

For the table of a Monte Carlo sensitivity function (the ss_aipe_*_sensitivity(), ss_power_*_sensitivity(), and ss_seq_c_sensitivity() functions), the record of its run: a list with attempted (the replications asked for), returned (those that produced a confidence interval, or a test), failed (those that did not), denominator (the replications the proportion, width, and coverage rows are taken over, which is returned), width_target_probability, and width_target_mc_ci, with any element the function adds (see the section on the record of the simulation on ss_aipe_cv_sensitivity). For the table of a standardized cluster randomized planner (ss_aipe_crd_es) that simulated a width, the record of the simulation of the design reported, with the same three counts, a denominator that is attempted for an assured width, and the elements that page lists (failure_reasons, width_mc_ci, and the totals of the search). NULL for any other table.

transformation, methods, rotation, structure

Family specifics where they exist: the transformation record of sem_exact_fit_bootstrap, the score methods of factor_scores as a plain character vector, the rotation and the fitted structure (covariance or correlation) of fa_exploratory.

footer

The lines a table of the fit families prints beneath itself, which state the version, the sample, and the qualifications in words. It is NULL for other tables, including one that prints a line of its own (the confidence set of nnt_from_smd is in that table's nnt_confidence_set attribute).

The names are part of DMAR's interface: a field is added when a new family needs one and is not renamed or removed within a release cycle without a deprecation.

Refusals

When DMAR will not run an analysis as asked, it stops with the reason and what to do instead. Every error DMAR signals on purpose, from the check of an argument to a fit that did not converge, is a classed condition: it carries, beside its own class, the class dmar_refusal and a code element with the name of its own class without the dmar_ prefix, so the refusals can be caught together with tryCatch(expr, dmar_refusal = function(e) ...) or each by its own class. An error that is not a dmar_refusal was not signaled by DMAR's own checks (it came from R, from another package, or from match.arg() for a choice that is not among an argument's values). The classes:

dmar_h1_unavailable

The unrestricted (H1) likelihood of a FIML or two-stage fit is unavailable (its affine-collapse diagnostic fired), so a fit measure, a two-stage criterion, or an EFA uncertainty that needs it is not computed; the condition carries the diagnostic as diagnostic. The same name is the class of the warning a function gives when it retains the constrained model's estimates and qualifies them instead; inherits(cnd, "error") tells the refusal from the qualification.

dmar_two_stage_rows_unavailable

A two-stage fit whose first stage read cases observed on an auxiliary variable alone could not be computed again with every case, so its fit measures are not reported; the condition carries the row counts as rows.

dmar_inadmissible

A fitted model given to sem_fit_measures, sem_residual_fit, sem_information_criteria, compare_sem, ecvi, or sem_exact_fit_bootstrap has an inadmissible solution: lavaan's post-estimation check, made on the model's own parameters when the fit has auxiliary variables, finds a negative variance estimate or a covariance matrix that is not positive definite. The condition's reason element names each failure once, in the order the check makes them: "negative_variance", "cov.lv" (the covariance matrix of the latent variables), "theta" (that of the residuals of the observed variables), or "psi" (that of the residuals of the structural part of the model), the last three the names lavaan::lavInspect() gives the matrices; variables holds the variables with a negative variance estimate; problems is a data frame with a row per failure and the columns reason, group (the label of the group, as lavaan gives it; NA for a fit of one group), level (1 or 2 in a multilevel fit; NA for a fit of one level), variable (NA for a matrix), and value (the negative estimate, or the smallest eigenvalue of the matrix); and auxiliary names the auxiliary variables set aside (empty without them). The group here is a label, a character string, where the refusals of sem_exact_fit_bootstrap below carry the group's index, a whole number counting the groups in lavaan's order.

dmar_two_stage_fixed_x

The residual based statistic of a normal theory two-stage fit, which sem_fit_measures, fa_confirmatory, and measurement_invariance report, is refused for a fit that conditions on observed exogenous variables (fixed.x = TRUE or conditional.x = TRUE); the condition carries those variables as variables, and the message says how to refit (fixed.x = FALSE, with conditional.x = FALSE too for a fit made with conditional.x = TRUE) and on which rows to keep the fit's estimates.

dmar_exact_fit_bootstrap_scope

A fit that sem_exact_fit_bootstrap does not take. The condition's reason element says why: "summary_data" (a fit to summary statistics), "ordered" (ordered indicators, named in variables), "estimator" (an estimator other than maximum likelihood, given as estimator), "two_level", "cluster" (a cluster variable, given as cluster), "weights" (sampling weights), "two_stage" (two-stage estimation), "fixed_x" (a fit conditional on observed exogenous variables, named in variables), "missing_without_fiml" (missing values left in the analysis data of a fit not made by FIML, as under pairwise deletion, with the group's index as group), or "no_test" (no standard test statistic).

dmar_pattern_too_small

A missing data pattern with no more rows than observed variables, which the pattern-wise transformation of sem_exact_fit_bootstrap cannot use. The condition carries the pattern's index among its group's patterns, numbered in the order of their first rows (pattern), its rows (n), the number and the names of the variables it observes (p and observed), and the group's index (group).

dmar_transformation_undefined

The model based transformation of sem_exact_fit_bootstrap is undefined for a group's data or moments. The condition's reason element says why: "not_positive_definite" (a covariance matrix, named in matrix, is not positive definite), "no_mean_structure", "nonpositive_variance" (a saturated variance is not positive), "singular_pattern" (the model implied covariance matrix of the variables a pattern observes, the pattern given as pattern, is singular), or, for the Newton iteration of the common transformation, "not_converged", "singular_jacobian", or "diverged" (with the step as step); group is the group's index.

dmar_log_ratio_undefined

ci_ratio_of_means or ci_ratio_of_means_paired was asked for the log ratio interval of a ratio whose numerator or denominator is not positive, where the logarithm is undefined.

dmar_bootstrap_needs_data

One of the same two functions was asked for a bootstrap interval from summary statistics, which cannot be resampled.

dmar_items_invalid

The items to analyze cannot be read from the input, whether they were named by items (in fa_exploratory, factor_count, parallel_analysis, measurement_invariance, and measurement_alignment), by the factors of fa_confirmatory and of the functions that fit through it (cfa_1, cfa_2, fa_bifactor, and fa_second_order), or by the model of measurement_invariance (a named list of factors or lavaan syntax) or of sem_sam. The condition's reason element says which check failed: "form" (not a character vector, or a name is NA), "unknown" (a name that is not a column of data or an item of S, the empty name included), "duplicate" (a name given twice), "count" (fewer than three items), or, with raw data, "data_names" (two columns of data share a name, or, with items = NULL, which makes every column an item, a column's name is empty or NA); and items holds the names at issue, empty when the failure is not about particular names. A model's structure is checked first and without this class (too few items on a factor, an item named twice among the factors), so from fa_confirmatory, the functions that fit through it, and the model of measurement_invariance the reason is "unknown", or "form" for a name that is NA, and from sem_sam "unknown" or "data_names"; the items of measurement_invariance and measurement_alignment can give any reason but "data_names". A target naming items the input lacks is dmar_target_invalid.

dmar_htmt_blocks_invalid

The blocks of htmt are not disjoint sets of distinct items under distinct names. The condition's reason element says which check failed: "construct_names" (a construct name given to two or more blocks), "repeated" (an item listed more than once in one block), "shared" (an item in two or more blocks), or "data_names" (an item whose name belongs to two or more columns of data); blocks names the blocks and items the items at issue (empty for "construct_names"). The refusal is made before any correlation is computed or any resample drawn. A block that is not two or more columns of data is dmar_argument_invalid.

dmar_target_invalid

The target of a target rotation in fa_exploratory cannot be read as one (or a target was given with another rotation, or none with a target rotation); the condition's reason element says which check failed: "rotation", "form", "names", "factors", "values", "none_specified", or "nfactors".

dmar_target_unidentified

The target does not identify the rotation: reason is "counts" (too few specified loadings in a column), "duplicate" (two columns specified alike), or "rank" (the unrotated loadings of a column's specified items have too low a rank), and factors names the columns at issue.

dmar_group_coverage

Under full information maximum likelihood, a group of measurement_invariance never observes a variable of the model (or an auxiliary variable), or never observes two of them together, so the ladder cannot be fitted; the condition carries the variables a group never observes as unobserved (a data frame with columns group, variable, and n_group, the cases of the group) and the pairs as pairs (columns group, variable_1, and variable_2).

dmar_bifactor_unidentified

A bifactor structure that fa_bifactor will not fit; the condition carries the factors and items at issue as factors and items, and the kind of refusal as reason: "unidentified" (the data cannot identify the structure), "names" (an item or factor placed twice, or names that clash), or "scope" (a structure outside the model the function fits, such as fewer than two group factors, which need not be unidentified).

dmar_second_order_unidentified

A second-order structure that fa_second_order will not fit; the condition carries the factors and items at issue as factors and items, and the kind of refusal as reason, with the values of dmar_bifactor_unidentified ("names" also for a first-order factor under no second-order factor, "scope" for an item on two first-order factors or a first-order factor under two second-order factors).

dmar_count_invalid

A number of resamples, permutations, or replications that is not a single whole number in its admissible range (2.5, a missing or infinite value, a vector, or a value below the stated minimum). The condition carries the argument's name as arg and its limits as min and max (NULL when no maximum is stated).

dmar_semipartial_r_incoherent

A full-model \(R^2\) smaller than the square of the semipartial correlation it is given with, which no data can produce, in var_semipartial_r, ss_aipe_semipartial_r, and ss_aipe_semipartial_r_sensitivity. The condition carries the two values as R2_full and r_sp.

dmar_bca_undefined

mediate was asked for the BCa interval of an indirect effect in data where the interval is not defined: the indirect effect is not estimable with one of the cases left out, so the jackknife acceleration has no value, or the bias correction or the acceleration is not finite. The percentile interval does not need these quantities.

dmar_scores_not_ordered

The observations given to an order-based effect size (vargha_delaney_A, cliff_delta, probability_of_superiority_paired) have no common order: an unordered factor, a character vector, an ordered factor beside anything but an ordered factor with the same levels, time differences in different units, a Date beside a POSIXct, or a class or shape that is not a numeric vector. The message says which case applies, what would have been computed, and what to supply.

dmar_studentized_statistic_undefined

statistic = "t" in randomization_test or randomization_test_paired for data whose observed standard error is 0 with a nonzero mean difference (two constant groups at different values; paired differences that are all the same nonzero value), where the studentized statistic has no value. The condition carries reason ("constant_groups" or "constant_differences"), alternative, the group sizes as n_1 and n_2 or the number of pairs as n, and p_value_mean, the exact p-value that statistic = "mean" gives.

dmar_hedges_correction_undefined

unbiased = TRUE in smd_c with a control group of 1 or 2, or in smd with \(n_1 + n_2\) of 2 or 3. On 1 degree of freedom the correction factor of Hedges (1981) is 0, so the corrected estimate would be 0 whatever the data; on 0 degrees of freedom the factor is not defined, because there is no standard deviation. The condition carries df.

dmar_assurance_invalid

An assurance given to ss_aipe_cv that is neither NULL nor a single number strictly between 0 and 1. The condition carries the argument's name as arg and the value given as value.

dmar_argument_invalid

A value, or a combination of values, that a function cannot use and that has no class of its own: the wrong type or length, a number outside its range, arguments that cannot be given together or that are missing together, a column that is not in the data, data or a fitted model the analysis does not cover. It is the class of every argument check in the package. The condition carries the name or names of the arguments at issue as arg. arg is NULL when the refusal is not about a named argument (a property of the data, a search that ran out of room), and in some checks whose message names the argument only in running text and not at its start. Among others it is given by ss_power_R2_change (a p_restricted that is not below p_full, squared multiple correlations that cannot belong to nested models, an effect stated in more than one way); by the partial and semipartial correlation functions for a p below 2; by smd and smd_c for unbiased = TRUE without the sample sizes, and by smd for a group of one with its own standard deviation; by ss_aipe_sc_ancova_sensitivity when a sample size is to be planned and no width is given; and by ss_aipe_R2_sensitivity, ss_aipe_cv_sensitivity, ss_aipe_cliff_delta_sensitivity, and ss_aipe_reliability_sensitivity when both the estimate to plan from and specified_N are given.

dmar_package_required

The analysis asked for needs a package that is not installed (or, for lavaan, a newer version than the one installed). The message names the package and how to install it, and the condition carries its name as package.

dmar_computation_failed

The arguments were accepted, and a computation made with them did not give a result: a search for a sample size or for a confidence limit did not reach its target, a model fitted for the analysis failed or gave no proper solution and no more specific class applies (dmar_not_converged, dmar_no_maximum, dmar_lavaan_error), a refit or a bootstrap failed, or a distribution could not be evaluated accurately at the values reached. The message says which and what to change.

dmar_internal_error

DMAR reached a state its own code should not reach. The arguments are not at fault; please report the call (see BugReports in the package's description).

dmar_desired_power_invalid

A desired_power that is not a single number strictly between 0 and 1, in any power planner (the ss_power_ functions). The condition carries the argument's name as arg and the value given as value.

dmar_effect_zero

A sample size was asked of ss_power_R2 or ss_power_R2_change for a planning value under which the null hypothesis is true (a squared multiple correlation, or a change in it, of 0), so that power equals alpha_level at every sample size; or of ss_power_reg_coef or ss_power_rc for a regression coefficient whose effect is 0 at the planning values, with a desired_power above alpha_level.

dmar_estimand_undetermined

An estimand asked for by name (estimand = "total" or "partial") of eta_squared, omega_squared, ci_eta_squared, or ci_omega_squared that the inputs do not determine, such as the total value from an F statistic, or a total for which no interval is formed. With estimand = "all" the same estimand is reported as NA. The condition carries estimand and the reason.

dmar_cost_ratio_invalid

A cost_ratio given to ss_aipe_two_phase_cost that is not a single positive number below 1. The condition carries the argument's name as arg and the value given as value.

dmar_two_phase_no_design

Planning values for which ss_aipe_two_phase_cost cannot represent the sizes of a design as whole numbers (a width too narrow for the standard deviation, or a proxy too inexpensive).

dmar_no_maximum

A factor analysis or structural equation model fit whose likelihood has no maximum: an error variance ran off below zero, and with it held further out (at ten times its estimate, or one model implied variance below it, whichever is further) the log likelihood is higher, or lower by no more than \(10^{-6}\) per case, so the likelihood is still rising or flat along that ridge and lavaan's optimizer stopped at a point its starting values and tolerance set; the estimates describe the optimizer rather than the data. It comes from fa_confirmatory (and cfa_k(), cfa_1, and cfa_2), fa_bifactor, fa_second_order, fa_exploratory (where it is also a dmar_efa_no_solution, with reason "no maximum"), measurement_invariance, measurement_alignment, the single-factor fits of reliability_omega and reliability_H, and the refits of ci_bifactor_indices and of reliability_H(fit = ), for every output. It comes as well from the fit of the analysis model to the population moments in ss_aipe_composite_sem, ss_power_composite_sem, ss_aipe_sem_path, and ss_aipe_sem_path_sensitivity, and from the lavaan fit that the OpenMx fits of mediation_mbco start from (DMAR's own, or one given as model). The condition carries the variables as variables (with their groups as group), their error variances where the optimizer stopped and where the check held them as estimate and fixed_at, the two log likelihoods as loglik, the check's tolerance and the number of cases as tolerance and N, and the lavaan code of the fit as syntax and lavaan_call, which the message prints (leaving the syntax out when it is too long to print, for R cuts an error message at 8170 bytes). Inside a bootstrap, such a replication is counted among those that raised an error, and the run goes on; in the Monte Carlo of a planner it is set aside as a replication that did not converge. A function that reads only the chi square of a fit, which does not depend on where on such a ridge the optimizer stopped, does not check it: ss_aipe_rmsea_sensitivity and sem_exact_fit_bootstrap.

dmar_null_R2_unsupported

ss_power_R2 was given a nonzero null_R2. The function plans the omnibus test only; the message gives the call to ss_power_R2_change for the test of an increment. The condition carries null_R2, true_R2, true_f2, and p.

The other refusals, each a dmar_refusal as well, are dmar_fiml_unbounded and dmar_fiml_unstable (the unrestricted FIML likelihood has no finite maximum for these data, or is numerically unstable; the condition carries the certificate as diagnostic), dmar_efa_no_solution (an exploratory fit that did not converge, is improper, or left its standard errors unavailable, as its reason element says; with the reason "no maximum" it is also a dmar_no_maximum), dmar_not_converged (a fit that did not converge, from fa_confirmatory, from measurement_invariance, where it carries the rung as level and that rung's lavaan code as syntax and lavaan_call, and from the functions that share the check of sem_fit_measures, those under dmar_inadmissible, and from any other function that fits a model, or is given a fitted one, and reads its estimates; the refusal of a fit given to average_variance_extracted, bifactor_indices, ci_bifactor_indices, or dmacs carries the function as fn and the number of iterations lavaan ran as iterations), dmar_lavaan_error, dmar_too_few_cases, dmar_htmt_undefined, dmar_H_improper (an improper solution given to reliability_H as a fit), dmar_fmi_saturated_singular, and dmar_fmi_not_inverted.

A warning is a qualification of a result that is returned. Every warning DMAR signals on purpose is classed and carries its code, so it can be muffled or read by class from withCallingHandlers(). Two classes are general: dmar_result_qualified (the result is returned and the message states what to know before using it: an approximation that was used, an assumption the data do not meet, a quantity reported as NA, cases or replications that were dropped) and dmar_argument_ignored (an argument that was given has no effect on this call, and the message says why). The others name one kind of qualification: dmar_fmi_not_at_maximum, dmar_heywood_warning (an improper solution: a negative error variance or a standardized loading beyond one), dmar_H_marginal_se (an interval for coefficient H from the marginal standard errors of the loadings alone), dmar_nc_F_clamp (a lower confidence limit of a noncentrality parameter set to 0; see ci_nc_F), dmar_two_stage_aux_only (cases observed on an auxiliary variable alone, which lavaan leaves out of its count), dmar_negative_reliability, dmar_two_stage_n, dmar_semipartial_r_no_R2_full, dmar_semipartial_r_rounded (a full-model \(R^2\) below the squared semipartial correlation by no more than rounding to two decimals allows; the condition carries R2_full and r_sp), dmar_nc_F_clamp_search (the sample size search of ss_aipe_R2 met the lower-limit clamp of ci_nc_F at intermediate sample sizes; given once per call, with the count as n_evaluations), dmar_replications_without_interval, dmar_replications_with_infinite_limit (replications of ss_aipe_cv_sensitivity whose interval has an infinite upper limit; given once per call, with the count as n_replications), dmar_uls_standard_statistic, dmar_bifactor_empirical, dmar_smd_undefined, dmar_meta_hk_zero_se (identical effect sizes under the Hartung-Knapp adjustment; the condition carries n_studies, estimate, se_conventional, lower_conventional, and upper_conventional), dmar_interval_degenerate (an order-based effect size whose estimated variance is 0, with reason "complete_separation" or "no_variation", the estimate, the sample sizes n, and limit_feng_cliff, the limit Feng and Cliff (2004) give for complete separation, which the function does not report), dmar_bootstrap_replications_dropped (a bootstrap or Monte Carlo interval dropped replications in which the statistic was undefined; the condition carries B, B_used, n_dropped, B_required, share_dropped, caution, and status), dmar_bootstrap_insufficient (more than half of the replications were dropped, or the adjusted positions of a BCa interval take more replications than were requested, and the limits are NA; the same fields, and for a BCa interval withheld at its adjusted positions also positions and B_suggest), dmar_bootstrap_exploratory (the result was computed from fewer replications than a reported result needs because options(dmar.bootstrap_exploratory = TRUE) is set; the same fields), and dmar_bootstrap_note (a BCa interval replaced by the percentile interval, or replicates that all have the same value, with every replication used), all four described in dmar_bootstrap. Each function's help says when.

A refusal is never a table: when a function returns a table, its result is eligible or qualified, never refused.

The errors dmar_bootstrap_cancelled and dmar_progress_error are not refusals. A bootstrap of the reliability family or of ci_bifactor_indices stops with the first when its progress callback returns FALSE, at the request of the application that called it, and with the second when the callback itself raises an error. Both carry done and total, the replications attempted and the number requested, and the second keeps the callback's own condition, with its class, as parent, so that an application can tell a failing callback from a failing analysis and still recognize a condition of its own behind it.

References

Feng, D., & Cliff, N. (2004). Monte Carlo evaluation of ordinal d with improved confidence interval. Journal of Modern Applied Statistical Methods, 3(2), 322–332. doi:10.22237/jmasm/1099267560

Hedges, L. V. (1981). Distribution theory for Glass's estimator of effect size and related estimators. Journal of Educational Statistics, 6(2), 107–128. doi:10.3102/10769986006002107

See also

dmar_tbl for the table class and its display, dmar_tidiers for tidy() and glance(), which put the same metadata into columns of a data frame.

Author

Ken Kelley kkelley@nd.edu

Examples

x <- reliability_alpha(holzinger_swineford[c("t1_visual_perception",
                                             "t2_cubes", "t4_lozenges")])
m <- dmar_metadata(x)
m$coefficient
#> [1] "alpha"
m$ci_method
#> [1] "bonett"
m$eligibility$status
#> [1] "eligible"

# Four items, so that the model has degrees of freedom to test (three
# would make it saturated, which sem_fit_measures() qualifies).
fit <- lavaan::cfa(
  "visual =~ t1_visual_perception + t2_cubes + t3_paper_form_board +
             t4_lozenges",
  data = holzinger_swineford, std.lv = TRUE, estimator = "MLR")
f <- dmar_metadata(sem_fit_measures(fit))
f$version
#> [1] "robust"
f$correction
#> [1] "nonnormality corrections of Brosseau-Liard, Savalei, and Li (2012) and Brosseau-Liard and Savalei (2014)"
